1.alt: The six stages of a 45-minute interview: requirements (0-5 min), estimation (5-10), API (10-15), high-level design (15-25), deep dive (25-40), wrap-up (40-45).

3.alt: Clients reach a load balancer that spreads requests over stateless app servers; sessions live in Redis and data in a primary database with read replicas.

6.alt: DNS resolution: the app asks the stub resolver, which asks a recursive resolver; the resolver walks root, then TLD, then authoritative servers, and caches the answer for its TTL.

10.alt: Live order tracking: the rider app sends location to a location service that publishes to pub/sub; the customer's WebSocket gateway, found via a registry, subscribes and pushes updates.

12.alt: Two-tier load balancing: an L4 load balancer spreads TCP connections over L7 load balancers that route by path to the UPI pool, bills pool, or CDN origin.

13.alt: A forward proxy sits in front of clients (employees going out to the internet); a reverse proxy sits in front of servers (internet users coming in to app servers).

14.alt: Stateless web servers behind a load balancer keep session state in Redis and uploads in object storage, so any server can serve any request.

15.alt: Cache layers from fastest and least shared to slowest and authoritative: app cache, CDN edge, gateway cache, in-process cache, Redis, database buffer pool, disk.

16.alt: Cache-aside: the app checks the cache; on a hit it returns, on a miss it reads the database and sets the cache with a TTL. Writes go to the database and then delete the cache key.

18.alt: Stampede protection: when a hot key expires, 50K requests per second miss and hit a single-flight guard; one request rebuilds from the database while others are served stale or wait briefly.

19.alt: CDN: viewers hit a nearby edge; edge misses go to an origin shield, and shield misses go to the origin, so the origin sees only a trickle.

20.alt: Redis Cluster: the client hashes the key with CRC16 mod 16384 to a slot; slot ranges are owned by primaries A, B and C, each with a replica.

21.alt: Choosing a database: if you need multi-row ACID or joins, choose SQL; otherwise pick by access pattern: key-value, document, wide-column or graph.

23.alt: B-tree versus LSM: a B-tree walks root to internal to leaf pages; an LSM tree writes to a WAL and memtable, flushes to SSTables and compacts them into deeper levels.

25.alt: Commit path: begin, write changes in memory and WAL records, check constraints, write the commit record, fsync the WAL, then acknowledge the client.

27.alt: Eventual consistency: a write is acknowledged by replica A and copied asynchronously to replicas B and C; a read from C before the copy arrives sees the old value.

28.alt: Leader-follower replication: writes go to the leader, which ships its log to a synchronous follower and an asynchronous follower; reads can go to followers, but your own recent writes are read from the leader.

29.alt: Quorum with N=3, W=2, R=2: a write is acknowledged by r1 and r2; a read asks r2 and r3, returns r2's newer value and repairs r3.

30.alt: Sharding: a key is hashed to one of 64 logical shards, and a routing map assigns those shards to 12 physical nodes; user 42 maps to shard 17 on node 5.

36.alt: A work queue: producers enqueue messages, workers process and acknowledge them, and after 5 failures a message moves to a dead-letter queue for alerting, inspection and replay.

37.alt: Kafka: a producer writes to topic partitions keyed by order_id; the notify group splits partitions between consumers, while the analytics group reads the same partitions with its own offsets.

38.alt: Hybrid fan-out: posts by normal users are pushed by fan-out workers into follower timelines; celebrity posts are stored once and merged at read time.

40.alt: Idempotency key: the first request inserts key K, does the work and saves the response; a retry with the same key finds it and returns the saved response without charging again.

43.alt: Saga: create order, reserve stock, charge, assign rider; if charging fails, compensations run in reverse: release stock, then cancel the order.

44.alt: Outbox: one transaction updates the order and inserts an outbox event; a relay or CDC reader publishes to Kafka, and consumers deduplicate by event_id.

45.alt: Raft: the client sends a write to the leader, which replicates with AppendEntries; once a majority (leader plus F1) has it, the entry commits, is applied and the client gets a reply.

46.alt: Fencing tokens: A holds the lock with token 33 but pauses; the lease expires and B gets token 34; when A wakes and writes with 33, storage rejects it because 34 was already seen.

51.alt: An API gateway handles TLS, auth, rate limits, routing and tracing, then forwards to a backend-for-frontend that calls profile, offers and orders services in parallel.

52.alt: Service discovery in Kubernetes: ready pods are registered as endpoints; a caller resolves payments.svc by DNS, and kube-proxy forwards to a ready pod.

53.alt: Circuit breaker states: closed until errors exceed 50 percent, then open (fail fast); after a cool-down it goes half-open, and if trial calls succeed it closes again.

54.alt: A distributed trace: the gateway starts trace 7f3a, orders takes 120 ms and payments takes 3.2 s because of a bank API timeout and retry; a p99 alert leads to the trace and then to logs filtered by trace_id.

56.alt: Disaster recovery: region A replicates asynchronously (about 5 s of lag) to a warm standby in region B; failover means detect, decide, promote, shift traffic, verify and reconcile.

57.alt: Authentication then authorisation: login issues a session or JWT; each request is authenticated, then checked for role, ownership or scope, and is either allowed or rejected with 403.

58.alt: OAuth authorisation code with PKCE: the app sends the challenge to the auth server, the user logs in and consents, the app gets a code and swaps it with the verifier for tokens.

59.alt: JWT verification order: check the algorithm is allowed, pick the key by kid from JWKS, verify the signature, check exp, iss and aud, then trust sub and scopes.

60.alt: Defence in depth: internet traffic passes a WAF and rate limiter, a gateway with TLS and authentication, a service that validates and authorises, and a least-privilege database user.

61.alt: Direct upload: the app records metadata as pending and returns a presigned URL; the client PUTs bytes straight to object storage, whose event triggers a worker that scans, makes thumbnails and marks the file ready.

62.alt: HDFS write pipeline: the NameNode maps file blocks to DataNodes; the client streams a block to DN1 on rack A, which forwards to DN4 and DN5 on rack B.

63.alt: Inverted index search: a query is analysed and fuzzy-matched ('panner' to 'paneer'), looked up in the postings list, scored with BM25 and the top 10 returned.

64.alt: MapReduce: input splits are mapped to (merchant, amount), shuffled by key, reduced to a sum per merchant and written out; a hot key is salted into sub-keys and combined.

65.alt: Stream processing: keyed Kafka events go to a stateful operator with checkpoints; a one-minute window closes when the watermark passes, and late events go to a side output.

66.alt: Analytics separation: the OLTP Postgres database feeds a Parquet lake through CDC; dbt transforms it into a warehouse of facts and dimensions that powers dashboards.

69.alt: Progressive delivery: deploy v2 dark, then turn the flag on for staff, 1, 5, 25 and 100 percent, then delete the flag; a guardrail breach at any step turns it off.

70.alt: Kubernetes reconcile loop: a Deployment owns a ReplicaSet that owns pods; the controller compares desired with actual replicas and creates or removes pods to match.

75.alt: URL shortener: redirects go client to CDN edge to redirect service to Redis to the KV store of code-to-URL; creates use a base62 ID generator; redirects emit click events to a queue for analytics workers.

76.alt: Pastebin: the paste service keeps metadata in Redis and SQL and the paste content in object storage; a cron job deletes expired pastes.

77.alt: Rate limiter: the gateway asks a limiter running a Lua token bucket in Redis, keyed by user, phone or IP; allowed requests reach the service, denied ones get 429 with Retry-After; a config service pushes rules to gateways.

78.alt: Unique ID generator: each service embeds a library that builds 64-bit IDs from timestamp, worker ID and sequence; the worker ID is leased from etcd or ZooKeeper so it is unique per process.

79.alt: Distributed KV store: any node can coordinate; it hashes the key onto the ring and writes to replicas A, B and C, succeeding with W=2 acks and reading with R=2 plus read repair; gossip, hinted handoff and Merkle anti-entropy keep replicas healthy.

80.alt: Distributed cache: the client library hashes keys on a ring to primary nodes A and B, each replicated to a standby; on a miss the app reads the database and sets the value with TTL plus jitter.

81.alt: Notification system: services publish events to a queue; the notification service applies preferences, caps and templates and routes to push, SMS and email queues, each drained by workers, with failures retried or sent to a DLQ.

82.alt: News feed: a post is saved and an event drives fan-out workers to write follower feed lists in Redis; reading the feed merges the Redis list with celebrity posts, ranks and pages by cursor.

83.alt: Twitter/X: tweets get a Snowflake ID and are stored, then go to Kafka for fan-out to timeline caches, search indexing and trends; reads merge the cached timeline with celebrity tweets and hydrate them.

84.alt: WhatsApp: A's message goes via gateway 1 to the chat service, which sequences and stores it, looks up B's gateway in the registry and delivers via gateway 7; if B is offline it stays stored and a push notification is sent.

85.alt: Instagram: the app uploads photos with a presigned PUT to object storage, whose event triggers resize workers that publish to the CDN; feeds come from a feed service with a cache of IDs and a metadata DB.

86.alt: YouTube: chunked uploads land in object storage, transcode workers produce renditions in parallel and the CDN serves them; the player fetches a manifest and then adaptive-bitrate segments.

87.alt: Netflix: the control plane (catalogue and personalisation) runs multi-region; playback fetches a manifest and then segments from ISP or edge caches; progress is stored by user and title for resume.

88.alt: Uber/Ola: driver apps send locations through a gateway into a city-sharded geo index; dispatch searches nearby cells, ranks by ETA, makes an offer and records acceptance with a conditional write; trip events go to Kafka for billing and analytics.

89.alt: Zomato/Swiggy: search and menus come from Elasticsearch and Redis; orders go to an idempotent SQL order service that runs a saga of payment, restaurant acceptance and rider assignment; rider pings update a geo index and status is pushed to the app.

90.alt: Google Docs: clients connect over WebSocket to the session server that owns the document; it orders and transforms operations, appends them to an op log and broadcasts them; snapshots go to object storage.

91.alt: Dropbox/Drive: the client chunks and hashes files, asks the metadata service which chunks are missing, uploads only those to object storage, then commits a version; a change event tells other devices to sync missing chunks.

92.alt: UPI-style payments: the app calls the PSP transaction service, which records a unique transaction reference in a SQL ledger and calls NPCI, which debits the payer bank and credits the payee bank; timeouts trigger status checks and daily reconciliation.

93.alt: Digital wallet: a transfer locks both wallets in a fixed order, checks the balance, debits and credits through the ledger and commits; top-up webhooks are deduplicated and a nightly job checks ledger sums against balances.

94.alt: BookMyShow: big launches go through a waiting room; the seat map comes from cache; a hold is a conditional update from FREE to HELD for 10 minutes, then payment moves it to BOOKED; a sweeper releases expired holds.

95.alt: IRCTC Tatkal: users pass a CDN and a token waiting room before the booking service conditionally decrements inventory per train, class and quota, issues a PNR and takes payment; a timeout releases the seat.

96.alt: Fantasy leaderboard: the scoring feed goes through Kafka to a points service that updates team totals in a Redis sorted set per contest; the rank service reads ZREVRANK and ZREVRANGE with a few seconds of caching; at match end a batch recomputes for prizes.

97.alt: Typeahead: search logs stream into an aggregator with decayed counts; a builder computes the top-k per prefix and publishes a snapshot loaded by in-memory suggest servers; the client debounces calls to GET /suggest.

98.alt: Web crawler: seeds feed a per-host frontier; fetchers obey robots.txt and politeness and store pages in object storage; a parser extracts links, which are deduplicated with a Bloom filter or seen-set before returning to the frontier.

99.alt: Product search: the SQL catalogue streams changes by CDC into Kafka, and indexers write to sharded, replicated Elasticsearch; a query is analysed, searched with filters and facets, ranked, cached and returned.

100.alt: Metrics monitoring: agents send to Kafka, ingest workers write raw points to a partitioned TSDB, rollup jobs build 1-minute and 1-hour aggregates, dashboards query through a cache, and an alert engine evaluates rules every 15 to 30 s and notifies with dedup and silencing.

101.alt: Distributed logging: apps write to a local file; an agent batches with a disk buffer and masks secrets, ships to Kafka, indexers write daily indices to a search cluster, and data ages from hot (7 days) to warm (30 days) to an object storage archive.

102.alt: Distributed message queue: producers append to the partition leader's segment and followers in the ISR replicate it; consumer groups read assigned partitions from an offset and commit it; a Raft controller holds metadata and old segments are deleted by retention.

103.alt: Distributed job scheduler: jobs live in SQL indexed by next_run_time; schedulers poll and claim due jobs with SKIP LOCKED and enqueue them; workers run them and record results in run history, retrying failures with backoff.

104.alt: Proximity service: an index builder turns the places DB into geohash or quadtree cells loaded by replicated in-memory search servers; a query looks up its cell and neighbours, filters by exact distance, ranks and hydrates details from a cache.

105.alt: Flash sale: static pages come from the CDN, a waiting room issues tokens and rate-limits, reservations atomically decrement stock buckets, then the order and payment follow; expired reservations return stock.

106.alt: Hotel booking: search uses Elasticsearch with filters and geo plus an availability cache; booking runs a SQL transaction that decrements every night where availability is positive, holds, takes payment and confirms with the supplier; events drive email, invoices and sync.

107.alt: Ad click aggregator: click servers assign a click ID and write to Kafka keyed by ad_id; Flink deduplicates and counts per minute of event time into an OLAP store; raw clicks also go to object storage for a daily batch recompute and reconciliation.

108.alt: Stock exchange: traders go through gateways that validate and check risk to a sequencer that numbers orders into a replicated log, then to an in-memory matching engine per symbol that emits trades to clearing and book updates to market data; a standby replays the log.

109.alt: Zoom/Meet: clients signal over WebSocket to a room service that assigns a regional SFU; media goes over WebRTC UDP to the SFU, which forwards the best layer to other participants; if UDP is blocked, a TURN relay is used.

110.alt: Hotstar IPL live: camera feeds go to encoders that build an ABR ladder, a packager cuts segments, an origin with a shield feeds several CDNs, and players pull segments from edges; login, entitlement and ads are pre-scaled.

111.alt: Online judge: submissions are stored by the API and queued per contest; workers run code in a sandbox with no network and strict limits, store the verdict, push it to the user and emit events to the leaderboard.

112.alt: Email service: inbound SMTP is checked for SPF, DKIM and DMARC, queued for spam and malware workers, and stored with bodies in object storage and per-user metadata indexed for search; clients read the inbox by cursor; outbound mail is queued with retries.

113.alt: S3-like object storage: the front end authenticates; on PUT, data is erasure-coded 8+4 across storage nodes in different racks or zones before the metadata service commits bucket/key to fragments; GET reads 8 of 12 fragments and verifies; scrubbers repair.

114.alt: Distributed counter: a like first inserts a unique (user, post) row, then the counter service increments one of 32 sub-keys; reads sum the 32 sub-keys with a 1-second cache; increments are also logged to Kafka for a durable store.
